decisions.rationale: Lead Charizard and Venusaur with Torkoal and Basculegion in back. Sun enables Chlorophyll Venusaur speed and Charizard Mega Y output to pressure the opponent's core.
decisions.notebook: Sun core: Mega Charizard Y + Venusaur + Torkoal. Back options include Basculegion and Arcanine/Corviknight.

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott and Gyarados to establish Prankster Tailwind or overwrite Drought with Rain Dance, denying the opponent’s sun-boosted Fire pressure while enabling Waterfall. Gholdengo offers strong spread Steel damage and Passimian pressures opposing Steel types with Close Combat while punishing Intimidate via Defiant.
decisions.notebook: Primary game plan: Whimsicott plus Gyarados provides immediate Tailwind/Rain Dance flexibility against sun. Preserve Gyarados when possible as the weather-reset option; use Gholdengo for spread Steel pressure and Passimian for strong physical Fighting damage and Defiant punishment. Hatterene remains the slower Trick Room mode for future games if the opponent commits heavily to Chlorophyll or opposing speed control.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolving Charizard sets Drought immediately, boosting Venusaur's Chlorophyll speed to outspeed the entire opponent field while guaranteeing a super-effective Sludge Bomb KO on Whimsicott (who has Focus Sash, but Sludge Bomb is special and Charizard's Air Slash can clean up or we can target Gyarados). Meanwhile Charizard uses Protect to absorb any incoming threat safely.
decisions.notebook: Sun core: Mega Charizard Y + Venusaur + Torkoal. Back options include Basculegion.

selection: Rain Dance (all adjacent, including ally Whimsicott)
decisions.rationale: Whimsicott guarantees Tailwind with Prankster, while Gyarados overwrites likely Mega Charizard-Y sun with Rain Dance. This preserves both speed control and Gyarados as the weather-reset option, reducing Fire damage and enabling stronger Water pressure next turn.
decisions.notebook: Core plan remains Tailwind plus Gyarados Rain Dance to counter sun, preserve Gyarados for weather control, and transition into Gholdengo or Passimian pressure. Keep Hatterene as the slower Trick Room mode in later games if the opponent relies heavily on Chlorophyll or speed control.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott is at 1% HP under Tailwind and outspeeds us, so Venusaur finishing it off with Sludge Bomb is guaranteed. Charizard uses Air Slash on Whimsicott to ensure it goes down even if Gyarados protects or switches.
decisions.notebook: Sun core (Mega Charizard Y + Venusaur + Torkoal) maintains weather control. Whimsicott fragile and easily picked off.

decisions.rationale: Charizard fainted and is forced to switch. Basculegion enters under Rain, enabling potent Water-type offense or Last Respects. Venusaur has no switch requirement and must pass.
decisions.notebook: Sun core (Mega Charizard Y + Venusaur + Torkoal) + Basculegion. Gyarados has Rain Dance, Wacan Berry, and Tailwind support. Watch out for Gholdengo, Passimian, Gliscor, or Hatterene in the back.

decisions.rationale: Encore Charizard-Mega-Y before it can repeat Air Slash, removing its flexibility and preserving Rain’s advantage. Gyarados then uses Rain-boosted, super-effective Waterfall into the locked target for the best chance to eliminate Charizard while Whimsicott has already fulfilled its setup role.
decisions.notebook: Maintain the Tailwind plus Gyarados Rain Dance core, then transition into Gholdengo or Passimian pressure. Preserve Gyarados when possible for weather control. Keep Hatterene as the slower Trick Room mode in later games if the opponent relies heavily on Chlorophyll or speed control.

decisions.rationale: Switch Whimsicott to Gholdengo, which is immune to Venusaur’s Sludge Bomb and blocks Sleep Powder while adding immediate pressure. Keep Gyarados in to preserve Rain and Tailwind, maintaining the speed advantage against Venusaur and limiting opposing weather options.
decisions.notebook: Rain Dance plus Tailwind is the primary fast mode; preserve Gyarados when feasible for weather control. Gholdengo is a strong transition after setup, especially into Venusaur’s Poison and Grass pressure. Retain Passimian for physical Fighting pressure. Keep Hatterene as the slower Trick Room mode in later games if Chlorophyll or speed control remains central.

decisions.rationale: Basculegion's Last Respects on Gholdengo hits for super-effective 2x damage boosted by Adaptability, and Venusaur's Earth Power hits Gholdengo for 2x super-effective damage. This picks up a potential double-tap on Gholdengo under Tailwind while dodging Gyarados's Wacan Berry and rain-boosted water attacks.
decisions.notebook: Sun core + Basculegion. Gyarados holds Wacan Berry, runs Rain Dance and Waterfall. Gholdengo holds Life Orb. Watch out for backline threats (Passimian, Gliscor, Hatterene).

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Shadow Ball plus Waterfall focuses Basculegion, the immediate super-effective threat to Gholdengo. Even though Shadow Ball alone is not a guaranteed KO, both attacks together secure the knockout if it does not Protect, while our Tailwind-boosted Pokémon act first. Removing Basculegion preserves Gholdengo and leaves Venusaur unable to damage it with Sludge Bomb.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Tailwind expires this turn, and Gyarados has Rain Dance while Passimian has Rock Slide threatening Torkoal. Protecting Torkoal blocks potential damage and spreads while Venusaur puts Passimian to Sleep Powder, neutralizing threats safely under sun.

selection: Rain Dance (all adjacent, including ally Passimian)
decisions.rationale: Gyarados should restore Rain first, removing Drought and sharply weakening Eruption while preserving the rain-control plan. Passimian then uses spread Rock Slide for super-effective pressure on Torkoal, neutral chip on Venusaur, and a chance to flinch either foe before they act.

Passimian is asleep this turn, so we target Will-O-Wisp on Passimian to ensure it gets burned when it wakes up (or remains neutralized), while Venusaur hits Gyarados or Passimian with Sludge Bomb to deal solid damage. Gyarados set Rain Dance last turn, but burning Passimian severely cripples its physical output.
decisions.notebook: Sun core + Basculegion. Gyarados holds Wacan Berry, runs Rain Dance and Waterfall. Gholdengo holds Life Orb. Passimian has Expert Belt and Defiant. Watch out for backline threats (Gliscor, Hatterene).

decisions.rationale: Double Torkoal: Close Combat is Passimian’s strongest super-effective option if it wakes, while rain-boosted Waterfall applies immediate super-effective pressure and can finish it. Removing Torkoal preserves Rain Dance’s value and prevents its Fire-mode pressure; Venusaur is less threatening under rain and can be handled afterward.
decisions.notebook: Rain Dance plus Tailwind remains the preferred fast mode, with Gyarados as the key weather-control resource. Preserve Gyarados when feasible. Gholdengo is a strong transition into Venusaur’s Poison/Grass pressure. Retain Passimian for physical Fighting pressure. Keep Hatterene available as a slower Trick Room mode when Chlorophyll or speed control is central.

decisions.rationale: Passimian is asleep and Gyarados threatens heavy water damage in rain. Torkoal uses Protect to shield itself from Gyarados's Waterfall while Venusaur hits Passimian with Sludge Bomb to finish it off safely.

Protect preserves Passimian from Venusaur while it is asleep and at low HP. Gyarados should Waterfall Torkoal, exploiting rain and its 4x-effective matchup to leave it near defeat while maintaining pressure and preserving Gyarados.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize Rain Dance and Tailwind-style fast control, with Gyarados as the key weather resource. Preserve Gyarados whenever feasible. Retain Passimian for physical Fighting pressure and consider Gholdengo into Venusaur’s Poison/Grass pressure. Keep Hatterene available as a slower Trick Room option when Chlorophyll or opposing speed control becomes central.

decisions.rationale: Gyarados is alone and Rain is active (2 turns left). Torkoal's Eruption is weak in Rain, so Will-O-Wisping Gyarados cuts its Waterfall damage in half. Venusaur hits Gyarados with Sludge Bomb for neutral damage. Protect is risky for Torkoal due to consecutive use failure.

Waterfall targets Torkoal, which is heavily damaged and vulnerable to a rain-boosted super-effective hit; removing it is the strongest immediate pressure. Gyarados is faster than Venusaur and should preserve the current Rain Dance rather than spend another turn refreshing it.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize Rain Dance and fast control across games, preserving Gyarados whenever feasible. Retain Hatterene as a slower Trick Room option if Chlorophyll or opposing speed control becomes central. Preserve physical Fighting pressure when Passimian is available and consider Gholdengo into Grass/Poison pressure.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur uses Sludge Bomb to finish off Gyarados (poisoned to 30% HP last turn, taking further poison damage). Torkoal is already fainted and can only pass.
decisions.notebook: Gyarados carries Rain Dance, Waterfall, Thunder Wave, and Protect with a Wacan Berry. Watch out for its Water-type offensive presence in rain.

decisions.rationale: Passimian is fainted. Gyarados outspeeds Venusaur in rain and Waterfall is guaranteed to KO its remaining 18% despite resistance, removing the final active foe before it can act.

reflections.summary: The opponent neutralized our sun strategy by leveraging Whimsicott's Tailwind alongside Gyarados overriding our weather with Rain Dance, exposing Charizard to an unfavorable matchup where it got Encored and KO'd.
reflections.adjustment: Bring Torkoal in the starting lineup instead of Charizard to better contest weather control against Gyarados's Rain Dance from turn one.
reflections.notebook: Gyarados carries Rain Dance, Waterfall, Thunder Wave, and Protect with a Wacan Berry. Watch out for its Water-type offensive presence in rain. Opponent pairs Gyarados with Whimsicott to immediately overwrite weather and set Tailwind.

reflections.summary: Won by immediately overriding Mega Charizard Y’s sun with Rain Dance while Tailwind and Encore control let Gyarados remove Charizard. The four were effective overall, but Passimian was largely neutralized by Sleep Powder and Gholdengo was a poor direct answer to Venusaur’s revealed Earth Power.
reflections.adjustment: Bring Hatterene over Passimian next game to add a slower anti-Chlorophyll/Trick Room option, while retaining Gyarados and Whimsicott for rain and speed control. Avoid treating Gholdengo as a safe Venusaur switch-in; no own Mega evolution was used or needed here.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s revealed plan is Mega Charizard Y sun paired with Chlorophyll Venusaur; Venusaur carries Sleep Powder, Sludge Bomb, and super-effective Earth Power, while Torkoal carries Drought, Heat Rock, Protect, and Will-O-Wisp. Basculegion has Adaptability, Mystic Water, and strong Water attacks. Continue prioritizing Rain Dance and fast control, preserve Gyarados, and consider Hatterene over Passimian when the sun/Chlorophyll core is central. Do not rely on Gholdengo as the Venusaur answer.
